timeout.rule: an engine behind a server gets no fixed time budget: each request may take floor_seconds plus slack times its expected time from the requests the engine served in this Eval (a prompt of n tokens at most t * max(1, n/m)^2 for a prompt of m tokens that prefilled in t; an output token at context c at most d * max(1, c/k) for one that decoded in d at context k; the tightest bound counts), floor_seconds alone before any; a request past it stops the Eval as hung

extra_repetition.rule: after a case's measured repetitions, one more when they disagree: their decode tok/s or time to first token spread (max - min over the median) by more than tolerance, or their outputs differ. A single measured repetition is compared with the warmup before it: when they disagree the case gets a second repetition, and a third when those two disagree in turn. The case's KPIs are the medians over all its measured repetitions, and the repeatable gate compares every output, the warmup's included. One repetition is enough on a quiet device: re-scored from their first repetition alone, 23 Qwen3.8-27B results kept their scores within 0.1% (4% at worst)

steady_state.rule: a case is measured at the speed it settles to: after its warmup_runs, a request that would be the case's first measured repetition stands as one more warmup when its decode tok/s and the request's before it spread (max - min over the median) by more than tolerance, until a request agrees with the one before it or the case has had max_warmup_runs warmups and decoded at least max_warmup_tokens tokens in them (at most max_warmup_requests warmups: an engine that adapts per decode window adapts by the tokens it decodes, so a short reply gets more requests to settle); that request is the first measured repetition, and extra_repetition and disturbed apply from it on. An engine that adapts to what it serves (a device cache filling with a case's experts, a profile settling) then has its adaptation measured as its speed instead of as a disturbed device; one still varying after max_warmup_runs is judged as before. Requests shorter than 100 ms, which vary with timer and scheduler jitter, and a case's first request, which has none before it, stand as measured. Each case records steady_state: its warmup_runs, how many the drift added, whether its first measured repetition agreed with the request before it (steady) and the drift, its decode tok/s over the case's first request's, less one. An engine whose warmup already agrees with its first repetition measures as before

speed.fresh_decode: reported, not judged: each case's first request in the part, before any warmup, decoded at its own speed; fresh_decode_score is their geometric mean beside the steady-state decode_score. An engine that adapts to a prompt or drafts from its earlier replies decodes a repeated prompt faster than a new one, and the steady-state score measures the repeated prompt
speed.stop_tokens: disabled; a stop token inside the output is reported as stop_crossed
speed.aggregate: median per case; the decode score is the geometric mean of the case medians
speed.noise: a KPI's run-to-run spread (max - min over the median of its score per repetition) is taken over the cases measured more than once; the result records how many (headroom.noise repeated_cases of cases). A case measured once has no spread and no standard error, and status says so instead of reporting none
speed.stalls: reported, not judged: every request records the host time each streamed chunk arrives (a served engine's stream events, an adapter's on_tokens calls); per speed case, the longest and the p99 gap between chunks after the first token over its measured repetitions (the larger where it has several), in ms and over the case's median round_ms. A speculative engine sends several tokens per chunk, so the gaps are between chunks, not tokens; an engine that delivers fewer than three chunks has the case's stalls unmeasured
speed.tool_calls: reported, not judged: on the speed cases whose prompts define tools (kinds tool-call and agent), the calls in the case's first measured output up to the model's first end token (stop tokens are disabled, so the output runs on past it), in the tool-call format the model's chat template renders: <tool_call> holding {"name", "arguments"} JSON (Qwen3, Hermes) or a <function=NAME> block with a <parameter=KEY> block per argument (Qwen3.5 on, Qwen3-Coder), plus the calls a server parsed itself (delta tool_calls). A call is valid when it parses and names a tool of suite/agent/tools.json with arguments it declares, of their declared types, and every required one; truncated when the output-token limit cut it (no end token before it closed), which is not counted as invalid; invalid otherwise. Another template format leaves the count unmeasured
speed.prefill_aggregate: prefill tok/s = prompt tokens / time to first token; the prefill score is the geometric mean over prefill_cases
speed.ttft_aggregate: the TTFT score is the geometric mean of the case medians of time to first token in ms, over every case
speed.disturbed: a speed case whose measured decode speeds spread (max - min over the median) by more than disturbed_spread stops the round: the device was disturbed (quiet rounds recorded at most about 10%); the result keeps what was measured, marked aborted, and has no status. When the case's measured repetitions decoded different replies (output_varies), only repetitions of the same reply are compared, and a case whose replies all differ is not judged disturbed
speed.output_varies: an engine whose greedy reply changes between repetitions decodes different texts, whose speeds differ by content, not by a disturbance: such a case is measured over its repetitions as any other (the extra repetitions run, since its outputs disagree) and records output_varies {replies, spread}, the distinct replies and their decode spread; the disturbed check compares repetitions of one reply only. The repeatable gate fails on it as before
speed.decode_text: with a pinned continuation (crit eval pin) and a replaying adapter, speed is measured by replaying that text; otherwise on each engine's own greedy output. Decode scores on different texts are not compared
speed.served: an engine behind an OpenAI-compatible server (crit eval run --url) gets every prompt as the chat messages and tools prepare froze next to its ids, under the server's own chat template; prompt and output lengths are the usage counts the server must stream, and a reply that ends before output_tokens (no standard field turns end tokens off) is measured on the tokens it has. The server prefills every request: a reply with cached prompt tokens fails. Prefill and time to first token include the server's HTTP and templating. lower_context needs the engine started again at the lower context: crit run eval, which serves the candidate itself, does that; a server Eval did not start cannot be, so there lower_context is not measured

sampled_speed.cases: the speed cases (suite/speed.json) again, output_tokens each with stop tokens disabled where the engine allows, one request at a time, after the greedy suite on the same engine
sampled_speed.sampling: the model's own defaults, frozen by prepare as prepared sampling: generation_config.json's temperature, top_p, top_k and min_p when it sets do_sample (temperature 1.0 when it sets none), temperature 1.0 with no filters when it does not sample; repetition, presence and frequency penalties stay neutral so every engine samples the same distribution
sampled_speed.request: every sampled request names every sampling field, so no engine default applies: the prepared settings, the filters they leave unset off (top_p 1, top_k 0, min_p 0), the penalties neutral (repetition 1, presence 0, frequency 0) and the seed; an engine that lists the fields it applies (crit serve's supported_sampling_parameters, an adapter's sampling_fields) gets only those, and one that cannot apply a field whose value is not neutral has no sampled decode
sampled_speed.repetitions: warmup_runs, then one measured repetition per seed of seeds.repetitions and none of speed.extra_repetition: different seeds decode different texts, whose tokens per round differ, so their speeds disagree by content; outputs are not compared. One seed is enough for the score: re-scored from one seed alone, 23 Qwen3.8-27B results kept their sampled decode score within 0.8%, while single cases moved by up to 23%; a case measured at one seed has no standard error, and status says so. The warmup stays and asks for the sampling check's log-probabilities, so the measured seed is a request without them: over 32 recorded results the warmup's time per target pass came 1.4% above its case's measured median at the median, but 4 to 8% above on every case of some engines, more than one seed's score moves. A repetition past seeds.repetitions takes the next seed (2, 3, ...). On request a case with one seed, or whose seeds leave its error above adaptive.target_se, continues at further seeds (adaptive)

adaptive.rule: every case reports its relative standard error (the spread of its repetitions' log decode speeds over the square root of their count) and the repetitions target_se would take at that spread. With crit eval run --adaptive-sampled (off by default), after the seeds' repetitions a case with one repetition, whose error is unmeasured, or whose error exceeds target_se gets one more repetition at the next seed (2, 3, ...) until its error is within target_se or it has max_repetitions; the case's KPIs are the medians over all of them and the result records the rule as sampled_speed.adaptive (null without it). A fixed repetition count (crit eval run --repetitions, a profile's sampled_repetitions) is not extended. A decode measured adaptively compares only with results measured the same way

sampled_speed.steady_state: speed.steady_state on round_ms (time per target pass) instead of decode tok/s, between replies decoded to their full length: a first measured repetition that disagrees with the request before it stands as one more warmup and its seed is asked again
sampled_speed.disturbed: a case whose measured repetitions' round_ms (time per target pass, which the text does not change) spreads by more than speed.disturbed_spread stops the round as speed.disturbed does; an engine that reports no rounds is judged on the greedy suite alone
sampled_speed.aggregate: median per case; the sampled decode score is the geometric mean of the case medians. From crit-eval-v7 it is the headline decode: real requests sample. The greedy speed suite's decode score is reported next to it
sampled_speed.engines: an adapter's engine samples through generate_sampled(prompt_ids, max_new_tokens, on_tokens, sampling); an engine behind a server gets the settings and the seed in the /chat/completions body (temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, seed). An engine that cannot sample has no sampled decode

sampling_check.rule: each measured speed case's sampled reply with log-probabilities: its sampled-suite warmup (seed sampled_speed.seeds.warmup), whose timing is unused, asks for them; without a warmup, or when the engine cannot serve one with them, one more sampled reply after the sampled suite at seed. The reply holds the emitted token's and those of top_logprobs alternatives at every position. Each position's processed distribution is rebuilt from the raw log-probabilities (temperature, then top_k, top_p, min_p), the unreported rest of the vocabulary as one last alternative holding the mass the reported ones leave, each of its tokens at most as likely as the last reported one. A position is judged when the reported alternatives determine that distribution: top_k keeps only reported tokens, or the top_p or min_p edge falls among them whatever the rest holds, or the rest's processed mass is known within tail_tolerance (exactly at temperature 1 without filters); other positions are reported as unresolved. Each judged token gets a randomized probability integral transform u = (mass of the more likely alternatives, the unreported rest last) + V * p(token), V uniform from the seeded generator
sampling_check.statistic: z = (mean u - 1/2) / sqrt(1 / (12 n)) over every checked token; u is uniform exactly when every token was drawn from its processed distribution, so a sampler favouring likely tokens (drafts accepted by greedy match) pulls z far below 0. The Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance from uniform is reported
sampling_check.gate: sampling: fails when |z| exceeds z_max or an emitted token falls outside its processed distribution at a judged position; unmeasured when the engine cannot sample or report log-probabilities, or fewer than min_tokens positions are judged
sampling_check.logprobs: the log-probabilities must be the model's own (before temperature and filters), the values the quality honesty check verifies for greedy replies

quality.modes: a run judges quality in one quality mode, recorded in requirements.quality_mode: preserve (the default) against the reference with exact activations; as_quantized, the mode for speed, against the same scores with a budget eight times preserve's (mode_thresholds): a floor that keeps out a broken engine (skipped layers, dropped experts, a collapsed path), not a ration on precision, so the stored format's own activations, lower-precision KV, heads and dense weights fit without per-group evidence. 4-bit activation math turns rounding-level differences into large KL swings (on Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4, two valid runs of the checkpoint as quantized differ by a prompt mean KLD of 0.045-0.08, p99 0.5-1.4), and the checkpoint run as quantized lands up to mean KLD 0.23 and p99 3.7 from the exact scores itself. In as_quantized, output differences that part at near-ties pass (forks) and the honesty check bounds the paths (honesty.modes); every other rule is the same in both. The mode also prices the limits prefill and the first tokens are measured against: preserve at the fastest 16-bit prompt activations (bf16, fp16_acc) or a faster arithmetic quality shows passing, as_quantized at the stored format
quality.rule: every quality text is a conversation rendered by the model's chat template with its generation prompt (prompt_ids), followed by the conversation's written answer cut to continuation_tokens (continuation_ids); prepare freezes both. crit eval reference scores every position of every text once per model, suite and reference version, teacher-forced on the prepared checkpoint (FP32), and stores each position's target log-probability and top_k. The engine scores the same ids through its serving paths (crit serve's chat-score-v1): every prompt position and the first continuation token from one prefill of the prompt, every later continuation token from its decode, each step forced to the continuation (drafts accepted only while they equal it, every correction and bonus token taken from it)
quality.conversations: the suite's quality conversations (suite/quality.json): one set

long.rule: one conversation per length, the i-th of conversations at the i-th of prompt_tokens: long.json's preamble, holding suite filler cut to fit, goes before the conversation's first user message so the prompt renders to about prompt_tokens tokens; each length is its own set, skipped when the prompt and continuation_tokens exceed the engine's max_context. The lengths' texts share their document, so a second text per length scored the same prefill again (crit-eval-v7 had three per length)
long.purpose: the engine prefills and decodes after prompts long enough to cross the thresholds where engines switch prefetching, prefill kernels or sparse attention

quality.paths: each set is judged on both paths the engine computes it with: SET/prompt, its prompt positions from the prefill (the arithmetic every reply's first token comes from, and the KV and state decode reads), and SET/served, the positions it serves: the continuation, its first token from the prefill's last position and the rest from decode

buckets.prompt: absolute position: 1-511, then powers of two (512-1023, 1024-2047, ...)
buckets.served: offset in the continuation: 1-31, then powers of two (32-63, 64-127, 128-255)
buckets.rule: reported per set and path so a threshold shows as a step; not judged

as_quantized.rule: the served and the scored paths may round apart where the engine's arithmetic depends on what it served before (forks), so the check bounds them instead of asking for the same values: each reply token's and alternative's log-probability within tolerance (forks.margin), each reply's mean difference of its tokens' log-probabilities within mean_tolerance, and a token in only one top_k list within tolerance of that list's edge. The served path then stays within that of the path quality judged

honesty.rule: the engine's greedy reply to each prompt of these sets over the chat API (logprobs and top_logprobs top_k; the server must render the prompt to its prompt_ids count, prefill it without a prompt cache and name every reply token by its bytes), then the same reply tokens scored as the continuation through chat-score-v1: every reply token's log-probability and every alternative in both top_k lists must agree within tolerance (natural log), and the top_k lists must hold the same tokens but those within tolerance of the k-th; it shows the scores come from the serving path. A set skipped for its context is not checked
honesty.long_reply: the long serving path is checked on the long-context curve's first point (context.curve_from): its request asks for logprobs and top_logprobs top_k, and its reply tokens are scored once as the continuation of its prompt, judged as above (the reply curve@POINT); unmeasured when the curve did not measure that point or the server names a reply token by no bytes. One long prefill instead of the two a reply of its own would cost

quality.kl: KL(reference || engine) at every scored position over the tokens in both the reference's and the engine's top_k, each reference token outside the engine's top_k in a bucket of its own with the engine's probability at most that of the engine's last listed token, plus one bucket for the rest of each distribution, at the smallest KL those bounds allow: a lower bound on the full-vocabulary KL that does not fall to 0 when the two lists share no token
quality.perplexity: ppl_ratio: the engine's perplexity of the scored tokens over the reference's
quality.top1: the share of positions where the engine and the reference rank the same token first

mode_thresholds.rule: a quality mode named here judges by its thresholds instead of thresholds (preserve's); a run's --quality-budget is laid over the mode's. as_quantized's are the cap its per-set allowance had (crit-eval-v0.3.0 to v0.4.x: the checkpoint's own quantization drift times 4, at most these), above which a checkpoint's drift no longer marks room an engine may spend but a format carried badly

allowance.rule: reported, not judged, and only on request (crit eval reference --allowance): when the checkpoint declares quantized activations, the reference scores the texts a second time with them quantized as declared and stores how far that run lands from the exact scores per set and path (allowance.json beside the scores; reference packages carry it when present): what the format itself costs. Runs do not read it; as_quantized's budget is the cap it was raised to at most

quality.judged: every set's prompt positions and served positions by the drift budget, each on their own, the prompt positions without the perplexity ratio (prompt_perplexity); quality passes when every set passes and the honesty check holds

prompt_perplexity.rule: SET/prompt reports ppl_ratio and judges kld_mean and kld_p99 only (its limits leave out ppl_ratio_max): the prompt positions predict the user's own turn, which a chat model gives little probability (Qwen3.8-27B puts nearly all of it on <|im_end|>; the long texts' prompt perplexity is about 3,000 to 5,300), so their perplexity is decided by the log-probabilities of tokens the model calls near-impossible, where the reference's own TF32 run moves single positions by up to 37 nats and its ratio to 0.77-1.40, and the same FP32 arithmetic cut into 4,096-token instead of 8,192-token chunks lands at 0.68 on long-4096. KLD weighs each position by the reference's probabilities and judges the same arithmetic; SET/served judges all three

probe.rule: the texts shorter than below_tokens are scored again first; when every set and path they hold has a spread below 1/margin of the level at which it would raise a limit (the budget over factor: kld_mean and kld_p99, and the perplexity ratio's distance from 1 on the served positions), the longer texts are not scored again and their sets are judged against the budget alone. Skipping can only leave a limit where it is, never raise one. The margin covers the growth of a dense model's spread from 4K to 32K tokens (at most 12x measured, Nanbeige4.3-33B) and saves the second run of the long texts, which hold most positions; a model that amplifies rounding shows it already in the short texts and gets the full pass

spread.rule: the reference scores every text of at least from_tokens tokens (0: every quality text, of every length) once more with its FP32 matmuls taking TF32 inputs (10-bit mantissas, about 1e-3 relative: the size of perturbation a BF16 or FP8 engine's arithmetic introduces, where FP32 rounding alone, 1e-6, under-estimated the effect a hundredfold on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) and stores how far that run lands from its stored scores, per set and path, by the same metrics (spread.json beside the scores). A model whose routing or recurrent state amplifies such a perturbation (a mixture of experts with near-tied routing, hard top-k selection, 4-bit activations whose rounding flips under the perturbation) disagrees with itself there by more than the drift budget, so a run judges such a set against the larger of the budget and factor times the reference's own spread (kld_mean and kld_p99; the perplexity ratio's distance from 1), and the result records both. A dense model's two exact runs stay within the budget, so nothing changes for it
spread.purpose: a perfect engine can match the reference no closer than the reference matches itself under an engine-sized perturbation

fail_fast.rule: sets are scored in the prepared order and judged as each completes; when a set's prompt or served path drifts a mean KLD over kld_mean_factor times the budget's kld_mean_max, the remaining sets are not scored (skipped, with the reason) and the run skips the long-context curve, exactness and the repeated follow-up and history requests (result stopped_early), since no later part can make it pass; the speed parts before quality stand

quality.budget: the thresholds are a drift budget to spend on speed, not a score to minimise; a run sets its own with --quality-budget

position_spread.rule: reported, not judged: each set and path's share of the drift budget over draws block-bootstrap resamples of its positions (the set's length in blocks of block consecutive positions, drawn with replacement from a generator seeded with seed), as the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles (budget_spread): how much the share depends on the positions the texts hold, since a few knife-edge positions decide the KLD p99

attribution.rule: reported, not judged, and only on request (crit eval run --attribute-drift): after quality, for each of the adapter's exact_variants (configuration overrides, each switching one matrix group or arithmetic choice back to exact), an engine opened with them scores the quality texts again, one engine at a time; per variant and set the budget it uses and its share, the full engine's budget used minus the variant's. Shares are not additive: the terms interact

quality.development: an engine opened in process by an adapter whose engine has score(prompt_ids, continuation_ids, top_k, prompt_rows) is scored and judged the same way, recorded as evidence development: its scores need not come from the paths it serves with and it has no served replies to check, so the quality gate stays unmeasured whatever the sets show; a served engine's are evidence served

exactness.rule: greedy speculative output equals the engine's own non-speculative greedy output token for token (the greedy speed suite); under sampling, sampling_check judges the distribution instead
exactness.engine: the plain greedy output comes from the speculative engine itself when its adapter declares plain decoding (info plain, generate_plain), else from a second engine opened with speculative false
exactness.modes: reported: agreement is shown and every emitted path is judged by the quality budget; required: any difference fails the gate

history.cases: the speed cases with the shortest and the longest prompt the engine holds
history.rule: each case's greedy output right after the engine built for the required context opens, before any other request, equals token for token its output after everything else that engine served (speed, held-out, quality, the long-context curve and retrieval)
history.gate: a gate whatever the exactness mode: a deterministic engine repeats a request whatever it served before, so it constrains no speed; in quality mode as_quantized a difference that parts at a near-tie passes (forks)

headroom.pass_floor: bytes read per model pass (adapter bytes_per_pass plus KV bytes at the case's context) / achievable device bandwidth; the bytes a pass reads from host memory at their own tier (tiers)
headroom.tiers: reported, not judged: the weights a pass and a prompt read from host memory, each byte priced at the tier it is read from (MoE-CAP's tiered cost model). An engine that declares host_bytes_per_pass ({link, cpu}) has its decode pass priced by it: the pass takes the longest of the device's bytes at its bandwidth, the link's at the probed host-to-device rate and both at host memory's read rate. Otherwise the tiers come from the model files' placement on the device at the required context (crit eval context): the resident weights the device cannot hold next to the required context's KV cache are read on every pass, and the routed experts by the share a token activates (experts_per_token of the experts, S-MBU's count) at the device cache's miss rate: one less the engine's hit rate (expert_hits over expert_reads in its decode telemetry, per case where it reports them) or, without one, the share of the experts the device holds (even routing, the pessimistic case); these bytes go by the faster of the link and host memory's read rate. A prompt of n tokens moves the resident bytes off the device and each off-device expert it touches at least once, E(1 - (1 - k/E)^n) of a layer's E experts at the run's miss rate, on the faster of the link and the CPU (host memory's read rate and the tokens' arithmetic on those bytes at the probed CPU rate): the prefill floor takes the longer of its arithmetic and that, the first-token floor the longest of its arithmetic, the device's bytes at its bandwidth and that, and the long-context curve's rounds and first tokens the same at each point. Experts the placement leaves on disk are priced as host memory, a lower bound. The result records the tiers (headroom.tiers), each case's expert_hit_rate and the pass's host bytes (headroom.host_pass)
headroom.fixed_decode: reported, not judged: each decode case's tok/s over one token per pass at a denominator the engine cannot move: the probed device bandwidth over the model files' bytes per pass (crit_eval.limits.context.pass_bytes) plus the KV the case reads at its context, at the protocol's KV precision (context.kv_precision), whatever bytes_per_pass the engine reports; per case and as the cases' geometric mean, beside the decode headroom. It exceeds 1 when speculation decodes more than one token per pass
headroom.prefill_floor: model FLOPs per prompt token by stored weight format / the device's best probed rate of that format (the larger of its cuBLASLt GEMM rate and its raw tensor-core rate), plus attention at the faster of the BF16 and FP8 rates and recurrent FLOPs at the BF16 rate
headroom.decode_ceiling: the larger of this drafter's speed of light and a drafter whose later drafts are accepted as often as its first, at floor costs, up to acceptance_ceiling_width
headroom.wider_draft: reported, not judged: an adapter that declares wider_draft ({width, config}) gets one more engine opened with that configuration after the run's own, which decodes each measured speed case once greedily for its drafts accepted per round; the projection then continues past the built width, each further draft adding what it added at the probed width
headroom.trace_parts: with a kernel trace (crit eval status --kernels), a speculative engine that reports no verify_ms and draft_ms gets them from the trace's decode: kernels classed draft over its draft steps, the rest over its rounds (GPU time), and the draft and verify gaps apart
headroom.ttft_floor: the larger of the prompt's compute floor and one read of the weights plus its KV writes at the device bandwidth

prompt_activations.rule: reported, not judged: the prefill and TTFT floors again with every quantized matrix group's prompt GEMMs taking each of these activation formats (BF16 at the BF16 rate, FP16 accumulating in FP16 at its rate, FP8 at the FP8 rate or for FP4 weights the FP4 x FP8 rate where faster, stored the stored-format floor) and with the engine's declared prompt_activations; a result whose engine declares them and whose quality is scored shows them passing (every SET/prompt path within its budget) or rules them out (one failing), and so does a baseline of the same model; the fastest shown passing is the reachable ceiling, with a prefill gap of its own

context.max_context: min(model limit, device limit): the positions config.json declares, and the KV cache that fits in the device's free memory (crit eval probe) after the VRAM headroom, the reserve, the weights read on every pass and the fixed state, at kv_precision, rounded down to granularity
context.engine: every engine is opened with context_tokens = the required context; the speed cases, quality and exactness all run on that build
context.curve: after the speed cases and quality, on the same engine, one greedy request per point fills the context (prompt + output): powers of two from curve_from below the requirement, each filling the share of the point the run draws for it (jitter), then the requirement itself, filled exactly; the prompt is the retrieval check's archive (long.json retrieval: suite filler text cut to fit with the retrieval facts at retrieval.positions of it) with long.json's curve_user request, which asks for the facts and then for a summary of the archive: each point decodes the engine's own reply, times it and judges retrieval on it, so one prefill of each long prompt serves both; every prompt is chat messages
context.capacity: the engine reports max_context of at least the requirement and completes the request at the requirement
context.devices: an engine on several GPUs is measured with a device file of all of them (crit eval probe --devices: each member's figures and every ordered pair's copy rate). Its memory is the members' together, each keeping the headroom and the reserve, for the max context; its floors price it as one device: the bandwidth of the faster split of a pass's bytes, tensor (each member reads its share, sized to its bandwidth, plus two all-reduces of hidden activations per layer, of which a ring moves 2 (N - 1) / N over the slowest link) or pipeline (members hold consecutive layers and a token runs through them in turn, plus N - 1 hand-overs over the slowest link), and each format's rate summed over the members that measured it; the result records the members and the split (device.device_set); device memory is sampled on every member and summed
context.device_memory: reported, not judged: the device memory free (nvidia-smi, the whole device) with the engine built for the requirement, after its load and after the curve filled the context up to it; the least of them, beside the capacity gate, and its change against a baseline
context.lower_context: the speed cases on an engine opened at lower_fraction of the requirement (never below the longest speed case), measured just before the engine built for the requirement; no case may decode slower or reach its first token later than at the requirement by more than its tolerance
context.tolerance_rule: per case and KPI, the larger of tolerance and the run-to-run spread of that case in either measurement

retrieval.rule: on the engine built for the required context: every curve point is a retrieval point, judged on its own reply (context.curve); every point of points below the requirement that the curve does not reach gets one greedy request after the curve, its prompt suite filler text with one fact (suite/long.json) at each of positions (fractions of the filler) and a question asking for all of them (prompt plus output equal the point). The output up to its first stop token, decoded with the prepared token strings, must contain every fact's answer verbatim. A retrieval request of its own is judged on its text alone: it may be served from a prompt cache, and its cached tokens are recorded
retrieval.gate: every point served and every answer found, on every candidate

followup.purpose: follow-up turns resend a conversation; an engine with a prompt cache prefills only the tokens it has not seen, and its cached path must answer as its fresh one does
followup.rule: right after the request history's first requests, one greedy request per turn of suite/followup.json in order: turn 1 its first user message after a document making the prompt about prompt_tokens tokens, each later turn the conversation so far with the suite's fixed assistant replies and the next user message, output_tokens each. Each turn may be served from a prompt cache: it reports time to first token, the prompt tokens the engine reports as cached (usage prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens) and the prefill rate of the rest (prompt tokens minus cached over time to first token); the KPIs are the geometric means of those over the turns after the first. After every other part the turns run again in order, and every turn's output must equal its first (gate prompt_cache). An engine without a prompt cache reports its fresh prefill and passes. An engine that declares it keeps no prompt cache (an adapter's info or crit serve's engine_facts prompt_cache false) is sent neither pass: each turn would be a fresh prefill the speed cases already measure, the part is recorded as not run with that reason (no_prompt_cache) and the gate passes. Cached tokens of 0 in the first pass declare nothing: a cache of whole prompts serves only the second pass. Skipped when the last turn does not fit the engine's max_context

forks.purpose: in quality mode as_quantized an engine may compute the same token with arithmetic that depends on what it served before: an expert on the CPU in one request and on the device in the next, a cache in another state, a prompt read from a prompt cache. Rounding can only flip a near-tie, so such a difference is allowed; a fork where one token clearly wins (a stale cache entry, a race reading another request's rows) is a defect either way
forks.rule: each output difference the repeatable gate (every distinct reply of a case's repetitions against its first), the request history and the repeated follow-up turns record is judged on the engine before it closes: the shared prefix plus the first reply's token at the first differing position is scored once through the engine's scoring path (chat-score-v1, top_k alternatives), and the fork is a near-tie when the other reply's token is among them within margin nats of the first's. In as_quantized the three gates pass a difference whose every fork is a near-tie; a reply that ends where the other goes on, a token outside the top_k, a wider gap or an engine that cannot score fail as before. Preserve judges every difference as before
forks.margin_rule: 2 nats: the other token is at least about an eighth as likely as the first. Rounding of 4-bit activations moves a position's log-probabilities by up to about 1-2 nats where two valid runs of a checkpoint as quantized differ most (their p99 KLD 0.5-1.4 on Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4)

heldout.purpose: speed gains must generalize: the held-out prompts (suite/heldout.json, several languages and domains) are outside the speed suite, and no engine choice may be tuned or selected on them
heldout.measure: on the engine built for the required context, after the speed cases: each prompt, cut to the length the run draws for it (jitter), decodes its own greedy output, output_tokens long, repetitions times; the median decode tok/s and tokens per round per prompt, and the held-out decode score as their geometric mean. 64 tokens once are enough for what the gate asks: the held-out score from the first 64 tokens' acceptance came within 1.4% of the 256-token score over 23 Qwen3.8-27B results
heldout.generality: against a baseline result that measured the held-out prompts, each at the length its own run drew (tok/s, which a small change in prompt length moves little): the held-out decode score may not fall by more than tolerance, and no held-out prompt may decode slower than in the baseline by more than prompt_tolerance; how far the held-out change trails the suite's is reported; without such a baseline the gate is unmeasured and the scores are reported

jitter.purpose: speed that holds for prompt lengths the suite does not name: an engine tuned to the suite's exact shapes (CUDA graphs captured at one token count, a tile or split choice for one prompt length, a prefill chunk that divides it) shows it as a slower held-out score and curve
jitter.rule: every run draws a seed (crit eval run --jitter-seed gives one; a resumed round keeps its journal's), and from it each held-out prompt and each long-context curve point below the requirement a fraction of its nominal length, uniform in fraction, from the seed and the prompt's id or the point alone (so neither the order of the parts nor which a stage runs changes a draw). A held-out prompt keeps the template around its user text and cuts the text, in tokens, so the whole prompt is that fraction of its prepared length, rounded up; an engine behind a server is sent the cut text. A curve point fills that fraction of the point, rounded up, with the same archive and request. The requirement's curve point stays exact (the capacity gate fills it), and the speed cases, quality, retrieval-only points, follow-up turns and the concurrency part keep their lengths. The result records the seed and every drawn length (jitter); a held-out prompt records its nominal_tokens and a curve point its filled_context, and their floors are priced at the drawn lengths

tracks.purpose: results a reader can compare like with like: the closed track fixes the choices that move scores for reasons other than engine work (MLPerf's closed division, SPEC's base), the open track keeps every freedom the protocol allows
tracks.closed: quality mode preserve; one configuration for every workload, loaded once for the run (no per-case or per-prompt-length settings); the checkpoint's own draft layers as the only drafter where it has them, no drafter trained or picked elsewhere
tracks.rule: reported, not judged: the result's track.closed holds Eval's checks of what a run shows, each pass, fail or unmeasured: quality_mode (the run was judged in preserve); one_load (Eval loaded the engine once for the run, and a server that reports its load count, crit serve's /health engine_loads, loaded no engine between the run's first request and its last); own_drafter (an engine that drafts reads per draft step no more than draft_tolerance above the checkpoint's own draft layers and the head their logits go through, the model files' draft_step_bytes, which a re-encoded head can only shrink; a checkpoint without draft layers leaves a drafting engine none of its own). qualifies is true when every check passes, false when one fails, null while one is unmeasured; the rest of the closed track (the configuration does not change with the case or the prompt length) is the card's declaration

concurrency.purpose: reported, not judged: how an engine that serves several requests at once does it, beside the single-stream suite it leaves unchanged; a served engine only (crit eval run --url, crit run eval), and only when the server reports max_concurrent_requests above 1 (crit serve's /v1/models card); an adapter's engine stays serial
concurrency.when: after every other part on the engine built for the required context, the request history's closing request included, so no single-stream figure or gate sees it; a staged run measures each level while it fits the budget (estimated from the level before it), a certified run and a profile measure every level
concurrency.clients_rule: the levels measured: those at most the server's max_concurrent_requests and with clients x (the longest pool prompt + output_tokens) at most the required context, the KV the requests hold at once
concurrency.loop: closed loop: the level's clients start together and each sends its next request when its previous one has ended, requests_per_client in all; client c's r-th request is the pool's prompt (c + r) mod its size, so a client never repeats a prompt and clients at the same step send different ones while there are enough
concurrency.pool: the speed cases with prompts of at most max_prompt_tokens, then the held-out prompts, each as the chat messages prepare froze; greedy, output_tokens long; the server prefills every request (a reply with cached prompt tokens fails, as in the speed part)
concurrency.aggregate: per level: completion tokens of every request over the level's wall interval (first request sent to last reply read; crit_eval.run.outcomes.validate_cohort, which disqualifies a level with a failed, missing or duplicated request or with fewer requests in flight at once than clients), the requests in flight at once at the peak, and per request the time to first token (p50, p95) and decode tok/s after the first token (p50)
concurrency.consistency: reported, not judged: each reply to a speed-case prompt is compared with that case's serial greedy reply from the speed part (its first output_tokens); a level reports the share of replies that match and each differing reply's first different token. A batch-invariant engine matches every one
concurrency.ceiling: per level, an aggregate ceiling of clients / the floor of one batched decode step of clients rows: max((the weights read on every pass + the routed experts the rows touch + rows x (KV bytes per token at the protocol's KV precision x the pool's mean context + the fixed state)) / bandwidth, rows x the active matmul FLOPs per token at each stored format's best rate + the rows' attention FLOPs); a layer of E experts routing k per token touches E x (1 - (1 - k/E)^rows) of them. The level's fraction is its aggregate over that ceiling

stages.purpose: a run without a profile measures in stages, each a prefix of the next, so an engine is measured as far as its own speed allows within budget_seconds: a slow first candidate gets the telemetry that says what to fix next in minutes, a fast one the full telemetry, and only the candidate that will ship pays for its required context
stages.budget: wall seconds from the run's start, loads included; after stage 1 the run goes on to the highest stage whose remaining requests, priced at the rates this engine measured (crit_eval.run.estimate), fit what is left; a part that would still pass the budget is skipped and named in stages.skipped. Stage 1 always runs. A certified run has no budget
stages.1: every candidate: the engine opened once at the requirement; each speed case once, with no warmup, a case after the first only while its expected time and stage 1's quality still fit the budget (one left out is skipped as over_budget, its coverage unmeasured); quality on every set whose longest text fits short_quality_tokens and still fits the budget, the honesty check included; the request history on the speed case with the shortest prompt; the device memory after the load against the KV cache the requirement needs (context.fit); decode time per output token fitted across the contexts measured and projected to the requirement (context.creep); the time to first token of the shortest prompt (speed.ttft_floor_ms)
stages.2: stage 1, then: the speed cases with prompts under long_prompt_tokens repeated (repetitions, with stage 1's request as their warmup, extended by speed.extra_repetition), longer ones kept at their one request; the follow-up turns once; the quality sets stage 1 left out; the curve's first point (curve_from), whose reply also serves the honesty check's long reply and retrieval there; retrieval at its points below the curve's first
stages.3: stage 2, then: the sampled suite at its first sampled_repetitions seeds after a warmup that serves the sampling check, no adaptive repetitions; exactness on exactness_cases speed cases; the held-out prompts when there is a baseline that measured them; the follow-up turns again. In crit-eval 0.4 stage 3 also ran the lower-context gate, which is now a certified run's
stages.certify: crit eval run --certify, the candidate that will ship: stage 3 whatever the budget, then one request at the requirement itself (the curve's last point and retrieval on its reply), which the capacity gate needs, and, after the engine closes, the speed cases once on an engine opened at the lower context, which the lower-context gate needs; without it capacity and lower_context are unmeasured and the curve stops at its first point

profiles.rule: a profile (crit eval run --profile NAME) fixes what a run measures so results from different machines and engines compare; the result records it as profile, and results of different profiles are not compared

hub.purpose: submissions to crit-hub: every engine measured at the same context, in a fraction of the full run's time
hub.curve_rule: the curve measures curve_from and the requirement only; the powers of two between them are interpolated from those two points (time to first token as a*n + c*n^2 through both, decode time per token linear in the context) and reported under context.interpolated, not judged
hub.retrieval_rule: retrieval is judged at retrieval_points and the requirement: 32,768 on the curve's own reply, 4,096 with a request of its own, the requirement on the curve's last reply; context.retrieval's points between them are not asked
hub.lower_context_rule: the engine is loaded once, at the requirement: the lower-context gate is unmeasured
hub.heldout_rule: the held-out prompts are not decoded: their generality gate needs a baseline, which a submission has none of
hub.sampled_repetitions_rule: the sampled suite runs two seeds, 1 and 2 (sampled_speed.seeds.repetitions, then the next seed); decode_se reports their spread
